result: {"lens":"safety_bypass","verdict":"NEEDS_FIX","summary":"Safety-bypass R4 review of WP-SCP-024 slice 024B. No CRIT findings. Three MAJ surfaces require fixes before fixpoint. (1) Three-gate break-glass Gate 3 accepts --i-understand-no-gate-2-verification, allowing re-arming the required check against a wrapper SHA never verified as a known-good release-tag; D-044 trust-model claim 'Gate 2 wrapper-SHA pin is explicit operator consent' does not hold when this flag is used. (2) Scaffolder test harness validates substitution values and YAML parse validity but does NOT assert the fork-PR refusal if: clause or workflow-level permissions ceiling (contents:read + statuses:write only); a template regression on either property propagates undetected to all five cascade adopters. (3) Prior-green-CI check's ?branch=${BRANCH} query returns 0 results for PR-triggered workflow runs (which execute on feature branches, not main), forcing operators to routinely use --i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci and normalizing the bypass flag — defeating the safety gate. Four MIN findings: Gate 2 SHA not verified as a release-tag; blocked-on-adopter-conflict negative assertion vulnerable to non-canonical --branch-protection-log path; --restore JSON accepted by shape without provenance verification; scaffold system-path denylist incomplete. Two nit findings: first-match **Target:** extraction and a restore-mode dead-code guard.","findings":[{"id":"R4-SAFE-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"--i-understand-no-gate-2-verification allows Gate 3 to re-arm the required check without Gate 2 completing. When Gate 1 has already disabled the required check and the wrapper is still pinned to a defective SCP SHA, this flag re-enables the gate against that defective SHA. D-044 trust-model claim 'Gate 2 wrapper-SHA pin is explicit operator consent to step backward from current SCP main' is inaccurate for this code path.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh lines 327-332: ACK_NO_GATE2_VERIFICATION bypasses --expected-wrapper-sha verification. ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 3 step 0 explicitly offers the flag as 'emergency re-arm'. D-044 rationale: 'Gate 2 wrapper-SHA pin is explicit operator consent to step backwards from current SCP main; Gate 3 ensures adopters don't stay un-gated forever' — no caveat for the escape hatch that voids this guarantee.","impact":"Operator using the flag after Gate 1 (disable) re-arms the required check against the still-defective SCP wrapper SHA, re-blocking adopter merges. The D-044 claim that the break-glass is 'auditable in git history' is violated: no Git artifact records that Gate 2 was verified before re-arming. Practical risk: operator responding quickly to a genuine SCP defect incident under time pressure.","mitigation":"ADOPT-001 §12.8 should add a WARNING under the flag: 'Using this flag re-arms against the current wrapper SHA. If the wrapper is still pinned to the defective SHA, the gate will re-block adopter merges. Complete Gate 2 first.' D-044 rationale should note the escape hatch. The emitted log entry should include a CAUTION line when ACK_NO_GATE2_VERIFICATION is set, making the bypass auditable."},{"id":"R4-SAFE-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"Scaffolder test harness (test_scaffold_downstream.sh) validates substitution field values and YAML parse validity but does NOT assert: (a) fork-PR refusal if: clause presence (mandatory per ADOPT-001 §12.7.1), (b) workflow-level permissions are exactly contents:read + statuses:write with no id-token:write or attestations:write. Template regression on either property propagates silently to all five cascade adopters.","evidence":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh lines 105-118: grep checks for branches, SHA, scorecard-emit; yaml.safe_load for YAML validity. No assertion for the if: clause or permissions block. templates/adopter-wrapper.yml.tmpl line 15: mandatory if: clause; lines 9-10: permissions block. DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criterion 'schema-validates against canonical wrapper shape from ADOPT-001 §12' is not met by the current test suite.","impact":"A template edit removing the fork-PR if: clause allows fork PRs to trigger policy-check on adopter repos, gaining statuses:write on fork-origin commits — the exact attack surface WP-SCP-020 020B closed. Adding id-token:write at workflow level exposes OIDC tokens beyond the job-scoped opt-in model in ADOPT-001 §12.7.15. Neither regression is caught before the cascade PR is opened and propagated to adopters.","mitigation":"Add assertions: (1) grep -Fq 'github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.event.pull_request.base.repo.full_name' wrapper; (2) grep -Fq 'contents: read' wrapper; (3) grep -vqF 'id-token:' wrapper; (4) grep -vqF 'attestations:' wrapper. These directly close the acceptance criterion 'schema-validates against canonical wrapper shape'."},{"id":"R4-SAFE-003","severity":"MAJ","claim":"enable-required-check.sh prior-green-CI query uses ?branch=${BRANCH} (adopter default branch, e.g. main). GitHub REST API branch param matches the HEAD branch of the workflow run. PR-triggered wrapper runs execute on feature branches, not main, so the query returns 0 results for ALL first-onboard invocations, forcing operators to use --i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci as a de-facto prerequisite rather than an exceptional cold-start override.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh ~lines 308-319: gh api 'repos/${REPO}/actions/runs?workflow_id=${WORKFLOW_ID}&status=success&created=>=${cutoff}&branch=${BRANCH}'. GitHub API docs: branch param = HEAD branch of the run. PR-triggered runs execute on the PR feature branch. Result: ?branch=main returns 0 green runs for all PR-triggered wraps. Safety bypass implication of correctness finding R4-CORR-001.","impact":"The prior-green-CI gate (verify wrapper has green-CI'd at least once before branch-protection mutation) is voided for all canonical first-onboard paths. --i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci becomes a routine step operators learn to always include, making it semantically meaningless as an exceptional bypass and normalizing bypass flag usage across the five-cohort cascade.","mitigation":"Remove &branch=${BRANCH} to match runs on any branch, or post-filter .workflow_runs[] on .head_branch after the API call. This restores the gate's intent: a first-onboard with a wrapper that has never green-CI'd returns 0 results and correctly blocks; re-arm where prior PR runs exist on any branch passes without the bypass flag. See R4-CORR-001 for the full correctness fix."},{"id":"R4-SAFE-004","severity":"MIN","claim":"--expected-wrapper-sha (Gate 3 verification) accepts any 40-char lowercase hex SHA without verifying it corresponds to a tagged SCP release. ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 2 says 'NOT a main-branch commit SHA' and 'the release-tag protection is the only audit anchor for known-good versions', but this requirement is enforced only by operator process, not technically.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh ~lines 293-307: extracts wrapper_pin from adopter wrapper and checks equality against EXPECTED_WRAPPER_SHA. No GitHub API call verifies the SHA has a corresponding v* tag. ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 2: 'Run: gh api repos/.../git/ref/tags/<release-tag> --jq .object.sha to obtain the release-tag SHA. Use this exact SHA... NOT a main-branch commit SHA... a non-tag SHA bypasses that integrity surface.'","impact":"An operator under stress or using tooling that returns a non-tag SHA (e.g. git rev-parse main) in Gate 2 passes Gate 3 verification while pinned to an unaudited commit. D-030 tag-protection (the audit anchor for known-good SCP versions per v* ruleset) is circumvented as a verification layer. The cascade re-arms against a SHA outside the audited release surface.","mitigation":"Add release-tag verification in Gate 3: after extracting wrapper SHA, call gh api repos/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-/git/refs/tags --jq '.[] | select(.object.sha==\"<sha>\") | .ref' and fail if empty. Or document in ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 2 that the operator MUST record the release tag name in the invocation log entry, making the bypass auditable."},{"id":"R4-SAFE-005","severity":"MIN","claim":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh normalize_path() strips only './' prefix; double slashes or non-canonical separators in --branch-protection-log survive. git diff --name-only returns canonical single-slash paths. If --branch-protection-log has '//', grep -Fxq fails to detect log modification, allowing the blocked-on-adopter-conflict negative assertion to silently pass even when the log was modified in the PR.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 89-91: normalize_path uses sed 's#^\\./##' only. Line 159: grep -Fxq \"$BRANCH_PROTECTION_LOG\" <<<\"$changed_files\". git diff output normalizes paths to single slash. Example: --branch-protection-log 'docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020//branch-protection-log.md' would not match 'docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md' returned by git diff --name-only.","impact":"In adversarial CI configuration (attacker controls --branch-protection-log argument), a cascade PR declaring blocked-on-adopter-conflict while having committed a log entry could pass the negative-assertion CI check. Practical risk is low: CI arguments are typically hardcoded in CODEOWNERS-protected workflow YAML. Nonetheless the check can be silently voided by a single argument mutation.","mitigation":"Replace normalize_path with full canonicalization: python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1])))' or equivalent, ensuring the value passed to grep -Fxq matches the canonical form git diff --name-only returns."},{"id":"R4-SAFE-006","severity":"MIN","claim":"--restore validates JSON shape (required keys and types) but not provenance. ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 1 instructs 'copy it to a local file first' but does not explicitly state 'verify the repo and branch values match the intended target'. A confused operator could apply the wrong invocation log entry's JSON (e.g. a different adopter's pre-state) and the script would accept it.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh restore_branch_protection() lines 377-453: validates repo, branch, before.required_status_checks, before.enforce_admins.enabled, before.required_pull_request_reviews types and structure. No log-file cross-reference, no check that repo/branch match the target of the current break-glass procedure. ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 1: 'copy it to a local file first' — no explicit provenance verification instruction.","impact":"An operator copying the wrong block from branch-protection-log.md (e.g. the second entry instead of the first) restores branch protection for a different adopter onto the current target. The degraded-state acknowledgement flags mitigate the worst case (enforce_admins=false, empty contexts) but not a well-formed JSON pointing to the wrong adopter repo.","mitigation":"ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 1 should add: 'Verify the JSON repo and branch values match the target adopter. The script validates shape only, not provenance.' Optionally, add a --restore confirmation prompt: display repo/branch being restored and require y/N before proceeding, making accidental wrong-JSON application visible."},{"id":"R4-SAFE-007","severity":"MIN","claim":"scaffold-downstream.sh system-path denylist covers /etc, /var, /tmp, /usr, /sys, /proc and macOS /private equivalents but excludes /root, /dev, /boot, /run, /mnt, /media, /opt. After readlink -f canonicalization (which resolves symlinks), an operator using a symlink inside their home resolving to an omitted sensitive path receives no warning.","evidence":"scaffold-downstream.sh lines 142-146: case block denylist. readlink -f at lines 133-136 canonicalizes before denylist check. Tests cover /tmp and /var/tmp (lines 199-212). Missing paths: /root, /dev, /boot, /run, /mnt, /media, /opt and macOS equivalents. Writability check at lines 138-139 provides partial mitigation.","impact":"On misconfigured systems or with elevated privileges, the scaffolder emits adopter artefacts to a sensitive directory without warning. Blast radius: adopter wrapper emitted to operator-unintended path. Practical risk low as /root and /dev are typically not writable without root; /opt and /run may be writable in container or dev environments.","mitigation":"Extend the case block denylist to include /root, /dev, /boot, /run, /mnt, /media, /opt and their /private/* variants. Or invert to an allowlist: only accept output-dir values under $HOME or an operator-configurable safe base path, with explicit override for non-home paths."},{"id":"R4-SAFE-008","severity":"nit","claim":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh uses re.search (first-match) for **Target:** extraction, not re.findall with an only-match assertion. A DISPATCH-NOTE with two **Target:** lines silently uses the first. For blocked-on-adopter-conflict, a fake first target with a valid TF-conflict reference could pass the TF-reference check while the real second target has no TF reference verified.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh lines 133-145: re.search(r'^[ \\t]*-[ \\t]+\\*\\*Target:\\*\\*[ \\t]+...', text, re.M) — first match only. Contrast: cascade-status parsing at lines 109-123 uses re.findall and validates exactly-one match, failing on 0 or 2. The asymmetric treatment is unjustified given that cascade-status already demonstrates the pattern.","impact":"A careless DISPATCH-NOTE that copy-pastes a prior slice's Target line while adding a new one silently uses the wrong target. For blocked-on-adopter-conflict, a carefully crafted fake-first-target with a valid TF-conflict reference fools the TF-reference check while the real adopter's conflict goes unverified. R1 correctness review is the compensating control; CI enforcement is weaker than it could be.","mitigation":"Switch to re.findall and validate exactly-one match: if len(matches) != 1: sys.exit(1) with 'ERROR: expected exactly one **Target:** match, found N: [values]'. Mirrors cascade-status parsing. Add a test case: DISPATCH-NOTE with two **Target:** lines must fail with this diagnostic."},{"id":"R4-SAFE-009","severity":"nit","claim":"enable-required-check.sh lines 324-332 (prior-log-entry marker check) run unconditionally in restore mode with REPO='' and BRANCH='', producing marker '— @'. If a log entry contained '— @' as consecutive characters (e.g. missing repo segment), the guard would fire unexpectedly in restore mode, requiring --expected-wrapper-sha or --i-understand-no-gate-2-verification. The check was designed for forward mode only.","evidence":"Arg parsing guard at lines 218-222 correctly rejects --restore with --repo or --branch. Lines 324-332 are outside the if [ -z \"$RESTORE_STATE\" ] forward-mode block (lines 261-322), so they execute in restore mode with empty REPO/BRANCH. prior_log_entry_marker=\"— ${REPO}@${BRANCH}\" becomes '— @'. Standard log format '— owner/repo@branch' does not contain '— @' as consecutive substring; theoretical only.","impact":"No practical impact: standard log entries follow '### timestamp — owner/repo@branch' and never contain '— @' as consecutive chars. Theoretical only. The guard running in restore mode adds noise but causes no real behavioral change given standard log format.","mitigation":"Wrap lines 324-332 inside if [ -z \"$RESTORE_STATE\" ]; then ... fi, or add [ -n \"$REPO\" ] guard at the block entry. This clarifies the code's intent — the prior-log-entry check is a forward-mode-only safety gate — and eliminates the dead execution path in restore mode."}]}
